applied.problem: Three rules are stated too absolutely: some parts are drawn in one view with a note; thin solid lines are also dimension and hatching lines; and shafts and bolts cut along their length are left plain too, not just ribs.

"Solid is an edge you can see" and "a chain line is a centre" are too absolute: thin solid lines also mark sizes and hatching, and a chain line thick at its ends is a cutting plane, as the next step says.

It says the box always unfolds round its back wall, where the front view lies, but in third angle the front view is on the front wall; it also says solid lines are edges and a drawing needs two views, both too absolute.
A floor plan often gives socket heights in a written note, so "it cannot show how high it is" is too absolute for an electrician who reads them.
A part drawing can run to several sheets, so "a part's views share one sheet" is too absolute.
